newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa prepares to advise Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: South Africa prepares to advise Kabila's Congo.

text.p: South Africa is preparing to offer technical advice and expertise to Laurent Kabila's new government in Kinshasa, but is unlikely to give direct financial aid, officials said on Thursday.

Ricky Naidoo, a spokesman for Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, said South Africa would coordinate assistance from African and other states to ensure that Kabila had immediate access to the advice and expertise he would need to start rebuilding the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire.

"Now that the first stage of the peace process is over, we cannot simply pack our bags and walk away. South Africa still has a critical role to play in terms of sharing our expertise," he told Reuters.
President Nelson Mandela's spokesman, Parks Mankahlana, said Mandela was keen to help Kabila establish control over the country's looted and vandalised government infrastructure, but he added:
"It's going to be largely technical assistance. We may not be able to offer any direct financial aid."
Mandela has already been criticised in the South African media and in parliament for the cost of his diplomatic efforts to guide Congo towards democracy.

South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said at the World Economic Forum meeting in Harare on Wednesday that Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad would head a task force to assess the new Kinshasa government's immediate needs.
"Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad is convening a team of people comprising a number of key government institutions and also representatives of our independent Reserve Bank," he said.
Manuel said it was important for the whole continent that the country should succeed following the ousting of former president Mobutu Sese Seko.
"We see it as fundamental as part of a wider vision for an African renaissance to put effort into the country now."
Naidoo said Kabila had asked South Africa to contact the World Bank on the technical assistance that might be available to help the country to rebuild its fiscal infrastructure.

At the same time, he said, joint United Nations and Organisation of African Unity envoy Mohamed Sahnoun would contact Western governments and funding agencies on direct financial help that might be available.
Apart from a senior central bank official, the composition of the South African team would be decided only after Kabila had named his government, Naidoo said.
